    ERROR: No matching distribution found for pyproject-fmt==2.30.3
```

I noticed that it required Python 3.11, so I switched, and the commit passed. Is it expected to fail for Python 3.10, while the DDT docs mention that the package supports 3.10?

## Steps to reproduce
1. Use Python 3.10 for the dev environment (e.g. `python3.10 -m venv .venv` and activate it).
2. Install dev deps and pre-commit (`pre-commit install`).
3. Run `git commit` (or `pre-commit run pyproject-fmt --all-files`).

Possible solutions that I can think of now:
- Remove support for 3.10 totally since Python 3.10 has reached its End of Life (EOL) on October 1, 2026 ([ref](https://devguide.python.org/versions/)) -- However, I don't think this is the ideal approach
- Fix the issue to support Python 3.10 for pre-commit hooks (probably revert to pyproject-fmt 2.30.2)
-  Keep it like this, but we need to mention it somewhere to use Python 3.11+ for contributing (may still support 3.10 for end users).

I first noticed this after upgrading to 8.0.0. When I load a page in Firefox, the toolbar briefly appears without its styling: the menu text is visible in the page, and huge blue theme icons fill the screen. A fraction of a second later everything looks normal. It's very brief, but hard to miss and quite distracting, even with the toolbar collapsed. We've narrowed it down to a plain HTML page with its content initially hidden. This test page is representative for an app built with VueJs which is also hidden on start. I can reproduce the flash with the template below, served through Django with the Debug Toolbar enabled and its default Shadow DOM setting. The page content becomes visible on `window.load`; the toolbar is inserted outside the hidden element. No toolbar assets are blocked or artificially delayed. ```html Hidden HTML toolbar reproduction

Hidden HTML toolbar reproduction

Content is hidden until the window load event.

``` In our local comparison, the version with its content visible from the start didn't show the same flash. I also haven't noticed it in Django admin. Although I first noticed this in 8.0, we checked older releases too. These are the results from loading the same project with each version and sampling the toolbar layout during loading: | Version | Configuration | Unstyled state detected | | --- | --- | --- | | 6.3.0 | Default | No | | 7.0.0 | Default | Yes | | 8.0.0 | Default | Yes | | 8.0.0 | `USE_SHADOW_DOM=False` | No | So it appears to affect 7.0 as well. Disabling Shadow DOM stops the flash on my page, and I'm using that as a workaround for now. The Shadow DOM change in [#2266](https://github.com/django-commons/django-debug-toolbar/pull/2266) looks relevant: could the toolbar be painted before its stylesheet is ready? Ideally its content would stay hidden until then. Environment: Firefox 156.0 on macOS, Django 6.1.1, Python 3.14.7, WhiteNoise 6.12.0. The flash is too short to screenshot by hand. **For the image below, we deliberately blocked the toolbar stylesheet to hold the unstyled state on screen.** The image illustrates the appearance; it was captured in a different browser, not during the normal Firefox load. During normal use, the stylesheet loads and the flash disappears by itself.

Howdy! 🤠

Currently we only pass the request to the `SHOW_TOOLBAR_CALLBACK`.

Inside the middleware we are capable of passing the response to the callback too, of course, with the caveat that the profiling must have already run. Thus, making the callback response dependent would be really only about “showing” the toolbar.

Why do I still think it's worth it? Header-based omissions.
Occasionally I have views, like iframes, where I don't want the toolbar to get in my way. It would be really cool if I could turn the toolbar on and off per request.

Anyhow, please let me know if there's anyone else with a similar use case, and I'd be happy to draft a mindful solution.

Cheers!
Joe

items.body: In #2216 [I observed that the toolbar state can appear inconsistent after using the History panel and switching to an earlier request](https://github.com/django-commons/django-debug-toolbar/issues/2216#issuecomment-5309871534). When switching, everything in the toolbar updates to show the data for the earlier request _except for_ the subtitle in the History toolbar item itself. In this example, after `/eligibility/` loaded, I opened the History panel and switched back to the `/` request: Everything else in the toolbar updates (the visible ones are things like like the Time, Request, SQL, and Templates), but the History item continues to show `/eligibility/`, which I found somewhat confusing. Then, when you close whatever full page panel you're looking at, the state of the app is still at the current request, but the data being shown in the toolbar (aside from the History item) remains showing the older request that had been switched to. Finally, one other minor issue is that if you switch away from the History panel and then reopen it, the older request you switched to is no longer highlighted. In discussion with @tim-schilling and @VeldaKiara at DCUS sprints yesterday, we agreed that the following should be done at minimum: - [ ] Change the History item's subtitle when switching to an older request - [ ] After switching to an older request, keep it highlighted if you leave the History panel and come back What needs further exploration: possibly introducing some additional notification to make it more obvious when the toolbar is showing data for an older request, and possibly introduce some kind of "take me back to the latest request" button.
items.title: UI state is somewhat confusing when viewing earlier requests

The `history_tr.html` template currently has a loop

`{% for key, value in history_context.history_stats.data.items %}`

Here, `history_context.history_stats.data` is captured via `HistoryPanel.generate_stats`: if request content type is `application/json`, it loads the JSON body. If the result dictionary contains key `items` itself, it uses the dictionary value under that key instead of calling dictionary `items()` method. If the value is, say, a string, the loop crashes.

      container_ips = socket.gethostbyname_ex(socket.gethostname())[2]

items.body:
The Cache panel currently determines whether a `cache.get()` operation is a hit or a miss solely by checking whether the returned value is `None`.

This leads to incorrect hit/miss reporting in the following cases:

### 1. Missing key with a default value

```python
cache.get("missing", "default")
```

The cache backend does not contain the key, so this is a **cache miss**. However, the Cache panel reports it as a **cache hit** because the returned value is the supplied default (`"default"`), which is not `None`.

### 2. Cached value is `None`

```python
cache.set("key", None)
cache.get("key")
```

The key exists in the cache, so this is a **cache hit**. However, the Cache panel reports it as a **cache miss** because the cached value is `None`.

## Expected behavior

The Cache panel should distinguish between:

* a missing cache key, and
* a cache key whose stored value is `None` (or any value equal to the caller's supplied default).

## Background

Django's cache framework recommends using a unique sentinel object when calling `cache.get()` to distinguish between a missing key and a stored value of `None`, see the highlighted guidance [here](https://docs.djangoproject.com/en/6.0/topics/cache/#:~:text=If%20you%20need%20to%20determine%20whether%20the%20object%20exists%20in%20the%20cache%20and%20you%20have%20stored%20a%20literal%20value%20None%2C%20use%20a%20sentinel%20object%20as%20the%20default%3A). The current implementation does not account for this behavior, which results in incorrect cache hit/miss statistics for the scenarios described above.
items.title: Cache panel incorrectly reports hits and misses for cache.get() when a default value is supplied or None is cached

items.body:
Description

The test tests/panels/test_sql.SQLPanelTestCase.test_param_conversion fails in the py312-dj60-sqlite, py313-dj60-sqlite, and py314-dj60-sqlite CI environments.

Root cause

PR #2385 added the condition django.VERSION >= (6, 2) to expect True/False in boolean parameters for non-PostgreSQL databases. The behavior change was actually introduced in Django 6.1, not 6.2. With pip_pre = True in tox.ini and dj60: django~=6.0 (which resolves to any 6.x release including pre-releases), the dj60 environments now install Django 6.1b1 (released June 24, 2026), which already passes True/False as boolean parameters on SQLite.

Why didn't PR #2385 catch this?

When PR #2385 was merged (June 16, 2026), django~=6.0 with pip_pre = True resolved to Django 6.1a1, which did not yet have this boolean behavior. Django 6.1b1, which introduced the change, was published 8 days later. Additionally, tox reuses existing environments unless --recreate is passed or declared dependencies change — so any local run after PR #2385 that had a cached environment with 6.1a1 would have continued passing, masking the issue.

This can also be confirmed empirically: Django 6.0.6 (the latest stable release) does not exhibit this behavior — boolean parameters are not passed for SQLite lookups. The change only appears starting from 6.1b1.

Fix

In tests/panels/test_sql.py, line 406, change:
and django.VERSION >= (6, 2)
to:
and django.VERSION >= (6, 1)

Steps to reproduce

2. Install tox: pip install tox
3. Run the failing test:
tox -e py312-dj60-sqlite --recreate -- tests.panels.test_sql.SQLPanelTestCase.test_param_conversion
▎ Note: Replace py312 with py313 or py314 depending on the Python version available in your environment. The issue reproduces on any of these versions as long as pip_pre = True is active (the default in tox.ini), which causes django~=6.0 to resolve to Django 6.1b1 instead of the latest stable 6.0.x release.

Expected result

Ran 1 test in Xs
OK

Actual result

FAIL: test_param_conversion (tests.panels.test_sql.SQLPanelTestCase.test_param_conversion)
AssertionError: Tuples differ: (['Foo', True, False], [10, 1], ['2017-12-22 16:07:01']) != (['Foo'], [10, 1], ['2017-12-22 16:07:01'])
items.title: Tests for SQLite environments with tox are failing for boolean parameters expected just in Django 6.2.

items.body:
I already verified the toolbar middleware comes after the gzip middleware, but any view that uses the `@gzip_page` decorator cannot use the toolbar.

Apparently `is_processable_html_response()` is returning `False` because the `Content-Encoding` shows up as `gzip`, but I thought the order of the middleware was supposed to solve that?
